findings.title: No module registry: module metadata is duplicated across six disconnected catalogs with no drift guard
evidence: apps/api/src/app.ts:174-233 — 60 route prefixes mounted by hand (first auth, last knowledge-base); no registry drives the mounts
packages/sdk/src/index.ts:347-421 — MCTClient declares 55 sub-APIs and assigns each in the constructor; adding a module means editing this class by hand
apps/web/lib/navigation/portal-nav.ts + apps/web/lib/navigation/admin-nav.ts — 63 portal and 57 admin module keys hardcoded in nav catalogs
apps/web/lib/module-config.ts:25-748 — separate per-module UI CRUD config (gov-changes, fs-isp, fn-backups, edu-sop, …) not linked to nav/permission keys
apps/web/lib/permissions.ts:45-133 — MODULE_LABELS covers only 41 labels while the permission catalog seeds 94 module keys (supabase/migrations/5302118_permission_matrix_full_catalog.sql)
apps/api/src/lib/entitlements.ts:21-41 — entitlement vocabulary contains "support" which is not a permission module key; the permission/nav key for that surface is "tickets"
scripts/openapi-audit.js:1-40 — the only cross-check is routes↔OpenAPI spec; nothing validates module keys across nav, permissions, entitlements, SDK and docs

prompts/mct-portal-os-expanded-60-modules-deep-prompts-pack/templates/api-route-template.ts:1-31 — route/migration/SDK/worker templates exist only inside the SHA-pinned historical prompt pack (prompts/PROVENANCE.md:1-8), not as live tooling
findings.impact: Adding or renaming a module requires coordinated edits in ~8 places (API mount, route, SDK class, nav, module-config, permission catalog migration, entitlement list, OpenAPI spec/docs) and drift is silent. The entitlement key "support" vs permission key "tickets" already demonstrates divergent vocabularies; future modules and AI agents cannot verify wiring from any single source.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a single module manifest (e.g. packages/config/modules.ts or a modules table) consumed by app.ts mounts, the SDK factory, nav catalogs, the permission-catalog migration generator, entitlements and docs; add scripts/check-module-registry.mjs to CI that fails when manifest keys, mounted routes, permission catalog keys and nav keys diverge; promote the pack templates into a live templates/ directory plus an "adding a module" checklist in docs/.
findings.owner: API principal engineer + web platform lead
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. Verified counts: 60 mounts, 55 SDK sub-APIs, 63/57 nav keys, 94 catalog module keys, 41 labels.

findings.title: Webhook UI advertises 11 event types but only 2 are ever dispatched; no event catalog exists
evidence: apps/web/components/admin/NewWebhookForm.tsx:6-18 — hardcoded EVENT_OPTIONS list of 11 events (ticket.updated, ticket.assigned, project.updated, document.created/updated, membership.created/updated, billing.invoice.paid/overdue, …)
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/webhooks/[webhookId]/WebhookDetailClient.tsx:8-20 — duplicate copy of the same 11-event list
apps/api/src/routes/webhook-management.ts:43-49 — the API accepts any string array (z.array(z.string())) with no catalog validation
apps/api/src/lib/webhook-dispatcher.ts:159-162 — dispatch filters endpoints by .contains("events", [event])

apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:522 — only emitter "project.created"; apps/api/src/routes/tickets.ts:183 — only emitter "ticket.created"; apps/api/src/routes/store/quotes.ts:536 — "project.created" again
grep for document.created|membership.created|ticket.updated|billing.invoice over apps/api/src, apps/worker/src, packages/sdk/src returns no emitter
findings.impact: A tenant that subscribes to 9 of the 11 advertised events receives nothing, silently — the endpoint filter simply never matches. The event contract cannot be evolved or versioned because there is no catalog to review, and consumers cannot tell supported from aspirational events.
findings.recommendation: Define a shared event catalog (typed union + payload schemas) used by the dispatcher, all emitters, the API validator and the web UI; add a CI test asserting every catalog event has at least one emitter and every emitted event is catalogued; document delivery semantics per event.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d; strengthens WH-P3-002 (event catalog) re-verified below. 4 dispatch call sites total, 2 distinct event names.

findings.title: Feature flags are a hardcoded static map with no managed service, change log, or targeting
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/feature-flags.ts:1-6 — DEFAULT_FLAGS is a code literal (new-onboarding, bulk-export-v2, sse-notifications, store-catalog)
apps/api/src/lib/feature-flags.ts:8-15 — resolution is only FEATURE_<NAME> env overrides, global (no per-tenant/per-user targeting)
grep for isFeatureEnabled|getFeatureFlags across apps/, packages/, scripts/ finds only self-references in feature-flags.ts — zero consumers anywhere in API, web or worker
grep for FEATURE_ across .env examples, workflows and deploy-do.yml finds no flag variables; git log shows the file unchanged since it was added (7a56f8dd)
findings.impact: Flag changes require a deploy, there is no audit trail of who changed a flag or when, and no staged/percentage rollout. Worse, the abstraction is dead code at 8d299b8d: no feature is actually gated, so env overrides cannot influence any behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Either delete feature-flags.ts and document that flags are not used, or move flags to a managed store/versioned config with an audit log and tenant/percentage targeting plus a kill switch; add a test that any flag referenced by code exists in the catalog.
findings.note: Re-verified at 8d299b8d: DEFAULT_FLAGS literal and env-only resolution unchanged since 9c0b88c; additionally the module has zero call sites, so the flag system currently gates nothing.

findings.title: No catalog-lint: referenced permission keys are not checked against the permissions table
evidence: .github/actions/unit-tests/action.yml:30-63 — the full guard list (openapi audit, docs counts/links, db-types --check, verify-rls, check-rls-predicate, review.md mirror) contains no permission-key check
scripts/ contains no permission-catalog lint; no test under apps/api/src/__tests__ reads supabase/migrations to compare requirePermission keys

Manual extraction at 8d299b8d: 43 distinct literal module keys referenced by requirePermission plus all 10 registerCrud factory modules (final/crud.ts:167-178) are present in the 94-key catalog (5302118) — the data is currently consistent, but only by hand
apps/api/src/routes/field-services.ts:257-264 — camera-calc CRUD is intentionally unguarded and has no catalog row; a future copy of that pattern silently escapes both RBAC and lint
findings.impact: A new route can reference a typo'd or unseeded permission key and pass CI; requirePermission then denies every non-bypass user at runtime (or, for an unseeded key with an admin bypass, silently over-grants). Renaming a catalog key has no way to find code references.
findings.recommendation: Add scripts/check-permission-catalog.mjs (CI) that extracts requirePermission literals and factory permissionModule values from route sources and fails when a key pair is absent from the migrations catalog; include the web-side permKey() usages; document the one intentional unguarded module (camera-calc) in an allowlist.
findings.note: Re-verified at 8d299b8d (previous row ACM-P3-002, area ACM; verified under the EVOL permission-catalog scope — the owning ACM domain may re-report this row, dedupe if duplicated). Current keys resolve; the guard is still absent.

findings.title: No committed event catalog or webhook documentation for consumers
evidence: No catalog file: grep for "event catalog" across the repo only matches audit artifacts under docs/audits/; docs/modules/webhooks.md covers inbound receivers only and docs/modules/webhook-management.md lists tables, not events

apps/api/src/routes/webhook-management.ts:43-49 — subscribers may store any event string; apps/web/components/admin/NewWebhookForm.tsx:6-18 — the only "catalog" is a hardcoded UI list duplicated in WebhookDetailClient.tsx:8
Only project.created and ticket.created are ever emitted (apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:522, apps/api/src/routes/tickets.ts:183, apps/api/src/routes/store/quotes.ts:536)

docs/modules/webhooks.md:39 still documents M365 as HMAC x-hub-signature against *_WEBHOOK_SECRET, while the implementation authenticates via M365_CLIENT_STATE (apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts:574-601)
findings.impact: Consumers (and future mobile/AI clients) have no authoritative list of events, payload shapes or delivery guarantees; documentation actively misdescribes M365 authentication. Event contract evolution is unmanaged.
findings.recommendation: Publish docs/EVENTS.md (or a generated catalog artifact) with event names, payload schema, sample delivery and retry/DLQ semantics; generate it from the same catalog introduced for the finding above; correct the M365 section of docs/modules/webhooks.md.
findings.note: Re-verified at 8d299b8d (previous row WH-P3-002, area WH; verified under the EVOL eventing scope — the owning WH domain may re-report this row, dedupe if duplicated). No catalog has been added; docs drift on M365 auth confirmed.

findings.title: API versioning policy is documented but not enforced (no Sunset/Deprecation mechanism; spec version unrelated to the app version)
evidence: docs/API_VERSIONING.md:11-16 — policy promises a Sunset header with a deprecation date, a 6-month support window and per-version migration docs
grep for Sunset|deprecat over apps/ finds only the doc; no middleware or route annotation emits Deprecation/Sunset headers
apps/api/src/app.ts:174-233 — every router is mounted once under /api/v1; there is no version negotiation, alias or deprecation registry
apps/api/src/openapi/spec.ts:4797 — info.version is hardcoded "1.0.0" while the repo VERSION file is 0.1.0 and apps/web/lib/version.ts reads a build-time artifact
packages/sdk/package.json:3-8,12-16 — @mct/sdk is private, source-only (main ./src/index.ts), version 1.0.0, no build/publish script, so there is no independently versioned client contract
findings.impact: Breaking changes cannot be announced or sunset per the documented policy, and consumers cannot pin a contract version. The platform's own web app is the only consumer today, but the documented policy is unverifiable and future mobile/AI/partner clients have no versioning seam.
findings.recommendation: Implement a deprecation middleware that emits Sunset/Deprecation headers from route metadata, tie OpenAPI info.version to the release version, add a breaking-change checklist to the release template, and decide (ADR) whether an external SDK is in scope.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. Docs/behavior mismatch reproduced from repo alone.

findings.title: Config model is duplicated per app; there is no shared env-schema package
evidence: apps/api/src/config/env.ts:19-143 — full zod env schema for the API
apps/worker/src/env.ts:5-107 — a second zod schema re-declaring the same classes of variables (NODE_ENV, LOG_LEVEL, SUPABASE_*, SMTP_*, SENTRY_*, JSM_*, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, …)
apps/web/lib/env.ts:3-16 — a third schema for NEXT_PUBLIC_* and runtime env with its own defaults
packages/config/package.json:5-9 — @mct/config exports only eslint.mjs, tsconfig.json and src/date.ts; no env module
INFRA-P2-006 history (previous run follow-up register) shows deploy-do.yml had to be manually kept in step with the app schemas for every integration/security variable
findings.impact: Adding one integration variable requires edits in up to three app schemas plus the deploy workflow; drift is only caught at boot (or not at all for optional keys). There is no single inventory of the platform's configuration model.
findings.recommendation: Extract @mct/config/env with shared schema fragments (supabase, smtp, sentry, integrations) and per-app composition; add a CI test that every key in the API/worker schemas is written by deploy-do.yml (and vice versa); generate docs/ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md from the schemas.

findings.title: Shared-package extraction is deferred: @mct/sdk and @mct/ui are source-only, and DB client setup is duplicated
evidence: packages/sdk/package.json:3-8 — main/types point at ./src/index.ts; version 1.0.0, private
packages/sdk/package.json:12-16 — scripts are typecheck/test only; no build or publish step, so the SDK cannot be consumed outside the workspace
packages/ui/package.json — same source-only pattern (no version, no build script)
apps/api/src/services/supabase.ts:58-93 (admin client + circuit breaker + metrics) vs apps/worker/src/services/supabase.ts — duplicated client construction
docs/arch/evaluation/db-package-evaluation.md — evaluation recommends a shared @mct/db package (weighted 6.8/10 with vs 5.8/10 current) but packages/ contains only config, sdk, ui
packages/sdk/src/index.ts:347-421 — 55 sub-API classes wired by hand in the MCTClient constructor
findings.impact: Duplication between API and worker persists for DB access, and the SDK cannot be published/versioned for external or mobile consumers. Every module addition also multiplies manual SDK wiring.
findings.recommendation: Record an ADR deciding package-extraction scope; at minimum extract a shared Supabase client factory (@mct/db) and add a build step to @mct/sdk; consider generating the sub-API wiring from the module manifest.

findings.title: Migration-strategy docs contradict each other and the tree (ISO vs sequential naming; seed.sql references)
evidence: docs/migrations/naming-guide.md:95 — "All new migrations should use the ISO-date format" (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS)
docs/SUPABASE_MIGRATION_WORKFLOW.md:9 — canonical workflow states schema changes live at supabase/migrations/NNNNNNN_name.sql (7-digit prefix)
ls supabase/migrations — all 134 files use the 5302xxx sequential prefix (latest 5302436); zero ISO-date files

docs/SUPABASE_MIGRATION_CHEATSHEET.md:41,68,141 — instructs `supabase db query < supabase/seed.sql`, but docs/SUPABASE_MIGRATION_WORKFLOW.md:12-14 states there is no supabase/seed.sql and seeds live in supabase/seeds/*.sql wired through config.toml
CHANGELOG.md Unreleased — documents "There are no down-migrations; rollback is restore-from-backup" (accepted decision, no reverse path to audit)
findings.impact: A contributor (or AI agent) following the naming guide creates a migration that violates the workflow doc and the tree's ordering; the cheatsheet points at a file that does not exist. Migration ordering is load-bearing for the hosted push, so conflicting guidance is a real operational hazard.
findings.recommendation: Pick one convention (the 5302xxx sequential prefix the tree actually uses), correct the naming guide and cheatsheet, and add scripts/check-migration-naming.mjs to CI (unique, monotonic prefixes; no duplicate numbers; documented gaps).
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. No duplicate prefixes exist today (uniq -d empty), but nothing prevents them.

findings.title: Roles, plan-to-module mapping, and status vocabularies are hardcoded with no parity guard
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/roles.ts:29-49 — CROSS_TENANT_KEYS/ELEVATED_TENANT_KEYS literals; comment (lines 24-26) says "kept in sync with the role catalog in supabase/migrations/5302128_role_catalog_expansion.sql"
apps/web/lib/roles.ts:20-31 — a third copy (PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEYS) with a "Keep in sync with" comment; no test compares the three lists

apps/api/src/lib/entitlements.ts:21-41 — plan effect is a binary subscription-active check over two hardcoded module sets; subscriptions.plan_name is free text (5302026_...:525) with no plan→module mapping table, so a new tier needs a code change

apps/api/src/validators/governance.ts:78 — change_requests.status accepted as z.string(); the column has no check constraint (5302071_governance.sql:14) while the UI offers a fixed 7-value list (apps/web/lib/module-config.ts:40-54)
grep counts: 76 z.enum(...) literals in apps/api/src; status option lists duplicated between validators, module-config.ts and DB enums
findings.impact: Adding a role, plan tier or status requires coordinated edits across code, migrations and UI; typos and omissions are silent (an unknown status passes the API and only breaks UI assumptions). The comment-enforced role sync is the exact pattern that produced earlier cross-tenant trust-model findings.
findings.recommendation: Make catalogs single-sourced: generate role-key constants from the catalog migration (or assert parity in a test), add a plan→module mapping table/config instead of two code sets, and move shared status enums into @mct/sdk with server-side zod validation plus DB check constraints.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d; covers the prompt's required hardcoded roles/plans/statuses check.

report:
# Platform Evolution and Extensibility Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`
- Repository: `github.com/MaineCyberTech/mainecybertech` (read-only worktree `/tmp/opencode/mct-audit-target`)
- Branch: `main`
- Commit SHA: `8d299b8d` (merge PR #168, 2026-10-11)
- Generated at: 2026-10-11
- Auditor: domain subagent (area EVOL), full-hardening rerun
- Area code: EVOL
- Output path: `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8/19_platform_evolution_extensibility.md`
- Scope limitations: static read-only review. Node.js is not installed on the audit host, so repository scripts (openapi-audit, guards) could not be executed; findings rest on source/config reading plus Python extraction of literals. No application or database was run; no production systems were touched.

## Scope

Reviewed for evolution/extensibility: module boundaries, domain model, shared packages, extension points, feature flags, permission extensibility, tenant/org model, API versioning, migration strategy, eventing/webhooks, integration framework, UI reuse, admin tooling, background jobs, config model, observability extensibility, docs for adding modules, AI-agent compatibility, package extraction.

Not reviewed in depth (owned by other domains in this run): RBAC correctness itself (ACM), webhook delivery/idempotency semantics (WH), RLS policy content (RLS/DATA), release/changelog process (REL), CI/supply chain (CI/SC). Cross-domain rows re-verified here are marked as such.

## Executive Summary

The platform is a Turborepo monorepo (3 apps + 3 packages) with real, working extension seams: a worker task registry with metrics and a central scheduled-scan table, server-side module entitlement enforcement sharing one derivation, a data-driven permission catalog with per-user overrides, route factories (`registerCrud`, `crudRoute`, `crudEndpoints`, `register*Routes`) that collapse repetitive CRUD wiring, a documented migration workflow with a dry-run plan artifact and post-push drift check, a coverage-gated OpenAPI spec, guarded agent documentation, and 75 module docs with feature/runbook pairs. These are genuine strengths and are why this domain scores 3–4 in most categories.

The recurring weakness is that module metadata has no single source of truth. A module's identity is spread across the API mount table, the SDK class, two nav catalogs, module-config, the permission catalog migration, the entitlement lists, and the OpenAPI spec. Today's data is mostly consistent (all 43 referenced permission keys resolve), but drift is silent — the entitlement key `support` already disagrees with the permission key `tickets`, and the webhook UI advertises nine event types the platform never emits. Adding a module or an event is therefore an unchecked, multi-file change with no scaffold or CI guard.

Prioritized next actions: (1) introduce a module manifest + `check-module-registry` CI guard and promote the pack templates into live tooling; (2) define a webhook event catalog and assert emitters in CI; (3) close the permission-catalog lint; (4) resolve the migration-docs contradictions and add a naming lint. Feature flags are dead code and should be deleted or rebuilt.

## Detailed Review

### Item: Module boundaries and registry

- Evidence: `app.ts:174-233`; `packages/sdk/src/index.ts:347-421`; nav catalogs; `module-config.ts`; `5302118`; `entitlements.ts:21-41`.
- What it does: routes are mounted manually under `/api/v1`; the SDK mirrors each route group as a class; the web app describes modules in three more lists.
- Current controls: OpenAPI coverage audit (`scripts/openapi-audit.js`) ensures routes appear in the spec; docs counts/links guards keep numbers honest; route-mount and tenant-scoping static tests guard new routers.
- Missing controls: nothing binds module keys across catalogs; no scaffold; templates live only in the pinned historical prompt pack.
- Risks: silent drift, incomplete module additions, agent/human confusion.
- Recommended improvement: single manifest + generator + CI guard (finding below).

### Item: Extension points (inventory)

- Worker tasks: `registerTask(type, handler)` (`task-registry.ts:19-25`) with success/failure/duration metrics and a no-handler counter; 28 registered types (`tasks/index.ts`); scheduled scans centralized with env gates and distinct offsets (`schedule-config.ts:27-55`).
- API CRUD factories: `registerCrud` (final), `crudRoute` (governance/field-services/security-suite/security-ops/batch/vendors), `register*Routes` (store). They differ: `final/crud.ts` uses `getSupabaseAdmin()` + `organization_id` query param, while governance/field-services use `getScopedClient(req, module, kind)`. A new module copied from the wrong factory inherits a weaker tenant pattern.
- Entitlements: `requireEntitlement(moduleKey)` + `GATED_MODULES` derived from one list.
- Permissions: `requirePermission(moduleKey, action)` resolved per request with admin bypass.
- Webhooks: event-name string filter.
- Metrics: prom-client registry with per-module counters (`lib/metrics.ts`).
- UI: `module-config.ts` + `module-record-actions.ts` generic update/delete; `AdminListPage`, `ModuleDetailPage`, `CrudForm`.
- Missing: an integration descriptor (each integration is hand-written), an event catalog, a module manifest.

### Item: Feature flags

- Evidence: `feature-flags.ts:1-15`; zero consumers; no `FEATURE_*` deploy vars.
- Assessment: not just unmanaged — currently dead. Verify/delete decision needed (EVOL–P3-001, still-open).

### Item: Permission extensibility

- Evidence: catalog migration `5302118` (94 module keys, role assignments for super_admin/admin/client_admin/technician/client_user), `lib/permissions.ts` (union of role_permissions across approved memberships + per-org overrides; super_admin bypass), `middleware/permissions.ts` (enforced on 225 call sites), `apps/web/lib/permissions.ts` (UI `can()`).
- Verification: Python extraction found all 43 literal module keys + 10 factory modules present in the catalog. No lint enforces this (ACM-P3-002 still-open).
- Risk: a typo'd key silently denies (or, combined with the admin bypass, hides the mistake).

### Item: API versioning

- Evidence: `docs/API_VERSIONING.md:11-16` (Sunset header, 6-month window, migration docs); no implementation; `spec.ts:4797` version `1.0.0` vs `VERSION` `0.1.0`; SDK private/source-only.
- Assessment: policy exists on paper only (finding below). Acceptable while the only consumer is the in-repo web app; a blocker for external/mobile/AI clients.

### Item: Migration strategy

- Strengths: workflow doc (`SUPABASE_MIGRATION_WORKFLOW.md`), pre-push dry-run plan uploaded as an artifact, fail-closed post-push drift check, `generate-db-types.js --check` in CI, RLS-predicate lint.
- Gaps: naming guide says ISO timestamps while the tree and workflow doc use 7-digit sequential; cheatsheet references a nonexistent `supabase/seed.sql`; no reverse migrations (documented decision); no duplicate-prefix lint (none exist today).

### Item: Eventing/webhooks

- Strengths: atomic idempotency claim, retry with backoff, DLQ, SSRF guard + pinned fetch, metrics, per-endpoint event subscription filter.
- Gaps: no event catalog; the UI advertises 11 events, only 2 are emitted; the API accepts arbitrary event strings; consumer docs missing/stale (M365).

### Item: Tenant/org model

- Strengths: `organizations` + memberships + roles + per-org `client_portal_entitlements` and `user_permission_overrides`; `assertResourceOrg` fail-safe 404; org-scoped admin resolution (`admin-scope.ts`); branding.
- Gaps: `organizations.settings` jsonb is an untyped extension point (single consumer: `status-page.ts:59` reads `status_page_enabled`); no org hierarchy (unknown if needed — no evidence of requirement).

### Item: Shared packages, config model, package extraction

- `@mct/config` is eslint/tsconfig/date only; each app owns its env schema (143/107/127 lines) with overlapping keys.
- `@mct/sdk`/`@mct/ui` are source-only private packages (no build/publish); `docs/arch/evaluation/db-package-evaluation.md` recommends `@mct/db` but it was never created; Supabase client setup is duplicated API↔worker.

### Item: UI reuse, admin tooling, background jobs, observability, AI compatibility

- UI: `docs/ui-kit.md` inventories shared primitives and app-local generics; `@mct/ui` has 7 components, 7 stories; adoption is real but narrow.
- Admin tooling: `AdminListPage` + `module-config` generic CRUD; admin nav guarded by `ADMIN_ROUTE_PERMISSIONS`; permission matrix UI.
- Jobs: registry + schedule config + scan lock; `WORKER_TIMEOUT` is not a real task timeout (RES-P2-002, owned by resilience domain).
- Observability: prom-client registry extensible per module; alert rules in `infra/digitalocean/alertmanager.tmpl.yml` (reviewed by OBS domain).
- AI compatibility: `AGENTS.md` is the single contract, mirrored to `review.md` and CI-checked (`sync-review-md.mjs --check`); prompt packs SHA-pinned with manifest verification; repomix config includes AGENTS.md as instructions. Strength.

IDs below are provisional; the aggregator assigns final IDs. Severity, status and evidence are authoritative.

### Finding ID: EVOL–P2-001 - No module registry: module metadata is duplicated across six disconnected catalogs with no drift guard

- Severity: P2
- Confidence: High
- Area: EVOL
- Evidence:
  - `apps/api/src/app.ts:174-233` — 60 route prefixes mounted by hand
  - `packages/sdk/src/index.ts:347-421` — 55 sub-APIs hand-wired in `MCTClient`
  - `apps/web/lib/navigation/portal-nav.ts`, `admin-nav.ts` — 63/57 module keys
  - `apps/web/lib/module-config.ts:25-748`; `apps/web/lib/permissions.ts:45-133` (41 labels vs 94 catalog keys)
  - `apps/api/src/lib/entitlements.ts:21-41` — `support` vs permission key `tickets`
  - `prompts/.../templates/api-route-template.ts` — templates only in the pinned historical pack
- What is happening: no artifact describes a module once; every catalog is edited by hand and only routes↔spec is machine-checked.
- Why it matters: adding/renaming a module is an unchecked multi-file change; drift is silent; agents cannot verify wiring.
- User/business impact: slower, riskier module rollout; features can appear in nav but be missing from SDK/permissions/entitlements.
- Security/privacy/reliability impact: a module missing from the permission catalog relies on the admin bypass or denies everyone; an entitlement key typo silently gates or ungates a surface.
- Recommended fix: module manifest consumed by mounts/SDK/nav/entitlements/permission migration generation; CI guard; live templates.
- Suggested validation: `scripts/check-module-registry.mjs` test fixture with a deliberately missing key must fail.
- Owner suggestion: API principal engineer + web platform lead
- Effort estimate: M
- Dependencies: permission-catalog lint (below)
- Status: open
- Endpoint/data path: n/a (platform-wide)
